rule.description: A fat operations interface (a struct of at least 6 capability members, every one a function pointer) is registered by file-scope ops tables; each implementor is flagged for every capability member it is forced to carry without providing it (member left NULL, zero, or omitted from the table initializer).
rule.implementation: Out-of-tree clang-tidy plugin (LLVM 18) distributed inside smell_check.sh; structural AST matching over file-scope table variables, no text matching. A translation unit that fails to analyze makes the whole check exit non-zero.

checks.description: A registered implementor (file-scope ops table) of a fat all-function-pointer ops interface carries a capability member that it leaves unwired.
checks.detected_relation: ops-table implementor -> capability member of the shared interface that this kind never provides
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The one-type-for-every-connection-kind interface exceeds its implementors' dependency boundary: each connection kind is forced to declare protocol capabilities that only other kinds exercise, which is the interface-segregation violation.

matches.evidence: Client connections are accepted sockets, so the interface's connection-establishment capability can never be provided; the client ops table carries the member as a NULL slot at src/client.c:1773.
An accepted client connection cannot experience outbound-connection failure; the capability is carried as a NULL slot at src/client.c:1773.
The SSL negotiation-character capability belongs to the server side (a client never opens a connection and negotiates SSL first); carried as a NULL slot at src/client.c:1773.
Backend server connections never choose a pool from a startup packet (that is client-login behavior); the server ops table carries the capability as a NULL slot at src/server.c:1000.
Backend server connections never accept cancellation requests of their own (only clients do); carried as a NULL slot at src/server.c:1000.
Cancel-forwarding peer connections never run the deferred oversized-packet delivery path; carried as a NULL slot at src/server.c:1023.
A peer connection never logs in against PostgreSQL, so the login-phase protocol state machine capability is carried as a NULL slot at src/server.c:1023.
A peer connection exchanges no queries, so the work-phase protocol state machine capability is carried as a NULL slot at src/server.c:1023.
A peer connection performs no authentication exchange with the peer, so the capability is carried as a NULL slot at src/server.c:1023.
A peer connection never completes a server login or forwards welcome parameters, so the login-completion capability is carried as a NULL slot at src/server.c:1023.
A peer connection never selects a pool from a startup packet; carried as a NULL slot at src/server.c:1023.
A peer connection forwards one cancellation request by explicit management code; the accept-a-cancellation-request capability is carried as a NULL slot at src/server.c:1023.

excluded.reason: Focused I/O backend vtable with 5 members, uniformly wired by both implementors (raw and TLS streams); it is below the fat-interface threshold and models the same table idiom without forcing any implementor to carry unused slots.
The connection-kind dispatch surface of this case lives entirely in src/; the vendored library holds no PgBouncer connection kinds and is outside the connection-operations responsibility area.
Not production code; no connection kinds are registered outside src/.
